- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.1) or near-zero, especially after recent peaks.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75) — model tends to overreact and overshoot by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, model often fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day after peak.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days before forecast, model often misses the downward correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is weak or volatile — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — model overfits recent highs; use 7-day rolling average for smoothing.
